title: Ivysaur Novice program review
summary: NH reviews the Reddit Ivysaur 4-4-8 novice program from a bodybuilding perspective. He likes its vertical pulls and higher pressing frequency but criticises the AMRAPs, the overhead press three times a week, the heavy compound-only days, the rushed progression and the missing isolation work, then proposes fixes that keep the template.
claims: Beginners make up about 95% of the lifting community, and many running powerlifting-style novice programs actually care about aesthetics
Novices do not recover faster than advanced lifters; they just lack the strength and work capacity to exert themselves as hard
For novices, frequency matters more for injury prevention than for hypertrophy
Three days a week is a good frequency for novice programs
Frequency also matters within the session: how long the program keeps you in the gym counts
Don't squat and deadlift on the same day at full exertion; if you pair a hip hinge with a knee flexion, keep the second in a higher, less taxing rep range
4x4 totals 16 reps, close to 3x5 (15) and below 5x5 (25); he prefers 3x5 and sees 4x4 as an odd compromise
With static rep ranges, getting 4 reps on both the first and last set means you sandbagged; for novices that is acceptable since they progress regardless
4x8 squats are risky for novices: mechanical failure comes fast, they grind ugly reps that ingrain bad patterns, and their muscles simply give out
Novices should do high reps, but in a range that keeps their form clean
OHP 4x8 against bench 4x4 doubles vertical over horizontal pressing volume, which is good for shoulder health and posture
Vertical pulls are key in novice programs for decompressing the shoulders and spine, especially when they bench often
Few novices can do 4x8 chin-ups; just do as many reps as possible for four sets
The vertical pull is the pattern with the fastest return to baseline: if you get 10 pull-ups you should get 10 again
Deadlifts should always lean toward intensity and good mornings toward volume; the bench sits in the middle
Heavy low-rep bench injuries come from a small error like flaring an elbow; high-rep bench injuries come from gradual breakdown as novices lose their arch and shoulder tightness
Deadlifts should be pushed, for example down to sets of 2 with one rep in the tank
The overhead press taxes the lower back for novices without a strong base of legs, glutes and core, especially right after deadlifts
Barbell rows after deadlifts and overhead press pile another tonnage bomb on the posterior chain; use cable rows instead
AMRAPs are rarely used properly; for hypertrophy an AMRAP should finish the job in a fatigued state, and an AMRAP top set that reaches 14 reps lands in an irrelevant intensity window
An AMRAP after 3x4 at the same weight works better because you are pre-fatigued, though four-rep sets still invite a risky extra rep
Doubling the progression rate after a strong AMRAP is a patch on poor programming that let trainees sandbag in the first place
Overhead pressing three times a week is too much: fitness culture tends to overcorrect a flaw (too little vertical pressing) into the opposite excess
Don't program weighted chin-ups for novices; let them master bodyweight first
Never AMRAP a deadlift; pulls from the floor are too easy to grind ugly reps on
Novice programs pile too many heavy compounds into one day; better to focus on one compound a day with variations, rep range variety and isolation
Adding 15 lb a week to the squat, 10 to deadlift, bench and rows, and 5 to OHP is rushed; novice progress is not a race
The program has no long-head triceps, forearm, trap, neck, calf or ab isolation, producing an unbalanced physique
Chin-ups are not a biceps builder; he has never seen a natural with big biceps from chin-ups alone, so curl
A good novice program introduces every movement pattern to build a wide base: slower progress but a higher ceiling
Linear progression is all a novice needs; AMRAP-based rate adjustments are unnecessary

To fix the template: move OHP so it appears on days 2 and 3 (4x4 on day 3), replace the third OHP with skullcrushers and curls, replace barbell rows with cable rows, face pulls and lateral raises, and superset with shrugs and ab work
exercises: do as many reps as possible for 4 sets; bodyweight before weighted
shoulder decompression; mainly an upper back builder, not biceps
too taxing after deadlifts and OHP for novices; replace with cable rows
fixed reps, never AMRAP; leave a rep in the tank
intensity lift; ugly reps easy to grind
long-head triceps work missing from the program
rear delt work to replace barbell rows
